title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is the last page (p. 6) of a typed English letter from 1984. The previous pages suggest it was sent to someone versed in hyperbolic geometry, since it mentions Thurston's ℓ_i, but the addressee is not identified on this page. The letter concerns 'surgery of conformal surfaces'. On the preceding page Grothendieck describes a conjectural model for admissible systems of discs on the sphere P^1 punctured at {0,1,∞}. Each such system would be a system of shrunken conical discs λ_i Q_i, with 0 < λ_i < 1, around the points s_i. Their common intersection would be three half-circles C_i joining two poles P^+ and P^-. This would give parameters λ_i for pants that are adapted to spherical geometry, and would identify the bordered moduli space as \tilde{MB} ≃ \tilde M × [0,1[^I. He complains that hyperbolic geometry of bordered conformal surfaces offers little beyond existence and uniqueness of the hyperbolic metric with geodesic boundary.

This page continues that complaint with two concrete questions. (1) Take a compact bordered conformal surface X of hyperbolic type, for example a pair of pants, and remove an open collar around its boundary to get a smaller bordered surface X' ⊂ X. How does the hyperbolic metric of X' (with geodesic boundary) compare with that of X? (2) If the λ-model is correct, find an explicit formula for the hyperbolic metric of a pant in terms of λ_0, λ_1, λ_∞. The letter then closes.

In modern terms, question (1) asks for a comparison or monotonicity principle for geodesic-boundary uniformizations under conformal inclusion of bordered surfaces. The standard Schwarz–Pick lemma does not apply directly. The geodesic-boundary metric is the restriction of the complete metric on the Schottky double, and the double of X' does not embed in the double of X. Question (2) asks for an explicit uniformization of pants in spherical or conical coordinates, which is generally not available in closed form.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page; it consists only of questions. The underlying λ-model from the previous page is conjectural, and Grothendieck explicitly flags it as possibly false.

ideas.what: Comparing the hyperbolic (geodesic-boundary) metrics of a bordered conformal surface X and the subsurface X' obtained by removing a boundary collar
ideas.modern_name: Monotonicity / Schwarz-lemma type comparison for hyperbolic metrics with geodesic boundary; relation of boundary lengths to extremal length and conformal modulus of collars
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related tools: Ahlfors–Schwarz–Pick lemma; collar lemma (Keen 1974, Halpern); Maskit's comparison of hyperbolic and extremal length (1985)
ideas.where_published: Possibly echoed loosely in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), section on Teichmüller towers and surgery of surfaces; not in this form

ideas.what: Request for an explicit expression of the hyperbolic metric of a pair of pants in terms of the 'spherical' disc parameters λ_i
ideas.modern_name: Explicit uniformization of pants / conformal-to-Fenchel–Nielsen coordinate comparison
ideas.usually_credited_to: No closed form known in general; numerical and partial results in the uniformization literature

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks how the geodesic-boundary hyperbolic metric changes when a collar is removed from a bordered surface. He wants a quantitative comparison, not just existence and uniqueness, as an ingredient for his conformal surgery of surfaces and for the bordered moduli space \tilde{MB} over \tilde M.
missed.quote: removing an (open) "collar" around the boundary, we get another surface with boundary X'- what about the relation between the two corresponding metrics ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Comparison results of this kind are partially known (extremal-length estimates, collar lemmas) but are not framed as a systematic theory for moduli of bordered surfaces. The question fits into the conformal-field-theory style 'moduli of bordered surfaces with collars' (Segal) that appeared a few years later. Still, this is an open-ended question rather than a result.

missed.claim: Conditional on his λ-model, he asks for an explicit formula for the hyperbolic metric of a pant in terms of the λ_i, i.e. a bridge between spherical and conformal parameters and hyperbolic Fenchel–Nielsen data.
missed.quote: it would be nice to have an explicit expression of the metric of a pant in terms of the parameters λ_i
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This would be part of relating the 'conformal surgery' coordinates to Thurston's length coordinates. It is an unanswered, though rather speculative, thread.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is the closing of a letter and only poses two natural, open-ended questions about hyperbolic metrics of bordered surfaces. These are interesting as context for Grothendieck's 1984 conformal-surgery program, but they contain no results or novel connections.
transcription_corrections: Typed 'aroun' is overstruck/corrected to 'around' in the original; 'boudary' has a handwritten 'n' inserted ('boundary').
'at' (typed as 'a*,') is struck out and replaced by handwritten 'between'.
'ypur's' is a typo in the original (for 'your's'); the transcription is faithful.
The handwritten page number '6' at top and '20' at bottom-left are archive and page markers.
